bracket: [Textbook answer-key error: the book prints \(\mathrm{Ans. : (-18.6\ kJ)}\). That is the answer for TWO moles of \(\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}\) — it is the value the book itself prints for Q.4 (xx), which asks about 2 moles of the same decomposition at the same temperature. This question specifies 132 g, and since \(M(\mathrm{NH_4NO_3}) = 80\ \mathrm{g\ mol^{-1}}\) that is 1.65 mol, giving \(\Delta n_g = 4.95\) and \(W = -15.35\) kJ. The key is self-refuting: the same reaction at the same temperature cannot do identical work for 1.65 mol and for 2 mol.]

[Textbook answer-key error: the book prints \(\mathrm{Ans. : (a = +983\ kJ\,;\ b = 0\ kJ)}\). The NUMBER for part (a) is correct but the UNIT is wrong by a factor of 1000 — oxidising one mole of HCl changes the gas count by only \(\Delta n_g = -0.25\ \mathrm{mol}\), so \(W = 0.25 \times 8.314 \times 473 = +983\) J, i.e. about \(+0.983\) kJ, not \(+983\) kJ. Part (b) is correct.]

[Textbook answer-key error: the book prints \(W = +10.13\) J and \(\Delta U = -609.9\) J. Those values follow from the litre-atmosphere conversion \(1\ \mathrm{L\ atm} = 101.325\ \mathrm{J}\), but the stem states the pressure as 1 BAR, and this chapter's own §4.4.2 gives \(1\ \mathrm{dm^3\ bar} = 100\ \mathrm{J}\) and uses it throughout Problems 4.1, 4.3 and 4.6. At 1 bar the work is exactly \(+10.0\) J and \(\Delta U = -610\) J. The difference is small (1.3%) but the book contradicts its own stated conversion.]

[Textbook misprint: equation (iii) is printed as \(\mathrm{H_2B_4O_7(s) \longrightarrow 2P_2O_3(s) + H_2O(\mathit{l})}\). A boron compound cannot yield a phosphorus oxide; the species intended is \(\mathrm{2B_2O_3(s)}\), which is the compound equation (i) produces, balances the boron and oxygen exactly, and is the only reading under which the Hess cycle closes on the target reaction. The stem is transcribed as printed and solved on that reading.]

[Textbook misprint: the prose of the question names the reactant "CIF" (with a capital i). The printed equation shows it correctly as \(\mathrm{ClF}\), chlorine monofluoride. The answer is unaffected.]

[Textbook misprint: the book's printed working shows \(48.62\ \mathrm{dm^3\ bar} = -P_{ext}(13\ \mathrm{dm^3} - 25\ \mathrm{dm^3}) = -P_{ext} \times 12\ \mathrm{dm^3}\). The second minus sign is wrong — \(-(13 - 25) = +12\) — and the book's own next line divides by \(+12\) to reach 4.052 bar. The sign has been corrected here so the derivation is self-consistent; the printed answer is unchanged.]

[Textbook misprint: the book's printed working ends "\(= 4955\ \mathrm{J} = 4.955\ \mathrm{J}\)", a false equality — 4955 J is 4.955 kJ, not 4.955 J. The unit has been corrected here; the value 4955 J and the conclusion that work is done on the system are as printed.]

[Textbook misprint: the book prints the reversed equation (iv) first as \(\Delta_r H^0 = -911\) kJ and then, four lines later, correctly as \(+911\) kJ. Reversing equation (i) must flip the sign, so \(+911\) kJ is right and the first printing is a misprint; it has been corrected here. Note also that the three values summed give \(-221 - 65.3 + 911 = +624.7\) kJ, which the book rounds to \(+624\) kJ.]

[Textbook misprint: the substitution is printed as \(T = \dfrac{-224\ \mathrm{kJ}}{-0.153\ \mathrm{J\ K^{-1}}}\). The denominator should read \(\mathrm{kJ\ K^{-1}}\) — the line immediately above converts \(-153\ \mathrm{J\ K^{-1}}\) to \(-0.153\ \mathrm{kJ\ K^{-1}}\) precisely so that it matches the numerator. It is preserved as printed; the value 1464 K is correct.]

[Textbook misprint: the reaction is printed as \(\mathrm{CH_4(g) + H_2(g) \longrightarrow C_2H_6(g)}\), which is not balanced — there is one carbon on the left and two on the right. The equation that balances and matches the hydrogen count is \(\mathrm{C_2H_4(g) + H_2(g) \longrightarrow C_2H_6(g)}\). It is preserved as printed because the calculation uses only \(K_p\), so the answer \(-100\ \mathrm{kJ\ mol^{-1}}\) is unaffected.]
